subjects.name: Database Management System
subjects.objective: A major rationale of a database system is to provide users with an intangible view of the data. That is, the system conceals certain details of how the information are put away and maintained. Thereby, data can be stored in compound data structures that permit competent retrieval, yet users see a basic and easy-to-use view of the data. The lowest level of abstraction, the physical level, depicts how the information is really put away and details the data structures.
course_outcomes: Apply techniques to identify business data issues and determine suitable requirements for resolving information-related problems.
Use appropriate methods to design and develop database systems that meet structural and performance requirements.
Apply data manipulation language (DML) commands to retrieve, modify, and manage data in a database.
Implement suitable physical storage and access methods to ensure efficient data retrieval and storage in database systems.
Apply normalization techniques to analyze and refine database schemas for improved data integrity and reduced redundancy.
